title: SB1178 (111th General Assembly): As introduced, allows a law enforcement officer or person who has a relationship with the respondent to petition a court for the issuance of an extreme risk protection order based on clear and convincing evidence that the respondent poses a significant risk of causing personal injury to the respondent or others by possessing a firearm. - Amends TCA Title 33; Title 38; Title 39 and Title 40.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Tennessee); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Tennessee text (Draft, 2019-02-06; official copy via the Internet Archive snapshot 20260513210638 of https://www.capitol.tn.gov/Bills/111/Bill/SB1178.pdf (LegiScan doc 1895798))

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1366(b)(1)): (1) Allegations that the respondent poses a significant risk of causing personal injury to the respondent or others by possessing a firearm;
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1366(f)): The temporary ex parte extreme risk protection order shall prohibit the respondent from purchasing, possessing, receiving, or having in the respondent's custody or control a firearm, firearm ammunition, or firearm accessories until the hearing.
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1366(g)): At the hearing on the petition, the court shall issue an extreme risk protection order if the court finds by clear and convincing evidence that the respondent poses a significant risk of causing personal injury to the respondent or others by possessing a firearm. The extreme risk protection order shall prohibit the respondent from purchasing, possessing, receiving, or having in the respondent's custody or control a firearm, firearm ammunition, or firearm accessories for a period of one (1) year.
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1366(h)): Upon issuance of an extreme risk protection order, the clerk of court shall forward a copy of the order to the Tennessee bureau of investigation for submission into the federal bureau of investigation's national instant criminal background check index.
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1366(k)): (1) A person commits an offense who purchases or possesses a firearm, firearm ammunition, or firearm accessory while subject to an extreme risk protection order. (2) A violation of this subsection (k) is a Class A misdemeanor.
